_comment: This is the per-engagement scope file described in Appendix D.2 and E.2 of the design document, extended by the Functional Agent design update (Section 5.1) with environment binding, capability binding, protected scope, mechanisms, governance and test scope. It is extracted from a signed-off Configuration Guidelines / Development Guidelines document -- never generated by an agent on its own. Copy this to scope.json and fill it in per engagement.
scope_revision: <bump this every time this file changes -- stamped onto every exact-change record that binds to it>

environment._comment: DEV isolation must be demonstrated, not assumed from the name (Section 1). Unresolved OCM/shared-data-source impact blocks execution -- see require_isolation_confirmed below.
environment.dev_environment_id: <e.g. DV920 -- the exact JDE environment name>
environment.ais_data_source_name: <the AIS/JDE data source this environment actually resolves to via OCM>
environment.isolation_evidence: <link or note: how OCM mappings were checked to confirm this environment's writes cannot reach another environment's business data>

approved_versions.notes: Example only -- default document type on a named sales order version.

spike_experiments._comment: A capability at Needs spike can still run, but ONLY as a bounded, explicitly approved DEV validation experiment (Section 2/3) -- never as an ordinary write. Each entry here authorises exactly one such experiment, for one capability, one target, one environment. Remove or expire an entry once the spike is complete; it is not a standing execution grant.
spike_experiments.capability_revision: <must match capability_catalog.json's current revision for this capability>
spike_experiments.expires_at: <ISO timestamp -- spike approvals should be short-lived>
spike_experiments.note: <why this specific experiment, and what it is meant to prove>

technical_agent._comment_authorized_object_types: Subset of the four Web-OMW-native types from Section 7.6 this engagement actually wants: ExternalFormApplication, DataStructure, Workflow, BusinessView. Empty until the feasibility spike (Section 10.2) and customer sign-off both say yes.
technical_agent.reserved_product_code: <one value from 55-59, agreed with the customer>

protected_scope._comment: Additional safeguards beyond the universal XJDE/ZJDE and 55-59 rules in scope.py, and beyond each capability's own protected_targets in capability_catalog.json -- engagement-specific things that must never be touched regardless of any other approval.
prohibited_interfaces: <e.g. direct database access, spec table writes>
prohibited_record_types: <e.g. specific master data tables this engagement has flagged as off-limits>

mechanisms._comment: Explicit allowlist (Section 1: 'Direct database/specification writes are disabled in the normal agent toolset... failure of a supported route never authorises this fallback').

governance.approval_policy: Exact-change approval per operation (approval.py), independent of and in addition to story approval (backlog.py)

test_scope._comment: A test/verification action (a report submission, order creation, etc.) is itself an action requiring its own permitted scope -- configuration approval does not implicitly permit posting, payments, outbound integrations, or unrestricted batch execution (Section 5.3).
approved_test_fixtures: <e.g. specific DEV test customer/order records safe to use>
permitted_test_actions: run_orchestration against the named acceptance test
